# Nirodhavāra (Ya 5.2.2)

**ID:** Ya 5.2.2
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Nirodhavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m4.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2) is the second subsection of the *Pavattivāra* (process section) within the *Saccayamaka*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma *Yamaka* [Anderson 1999]. In this section, the text analyzes the condition of beings who are reborn or pass away in various realms with respect to the cessation (*nirodha*) of the four noble truths in relation to one another [Anderson 1999]. In standard *Yamaka* style, this inquiry is carried out using paired questions applied across different temporal divisions—the present, the past, the future, and combinations of these time frames [Anderson 1999; Nyanatiloka 2007].

**Sources**

- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravāda Buddhist Canon (1999) — Description of the Pavattivāra of Saccayamaka and the structure of Nirodhavāra
- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, rev. 2007) — Temporal framework (present, past, future) in Yamaka nirodhavāra
- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics: The Making of a Philosophical Tradition (2005) — Significance of the pavattivāra (uppāda-, nirodha-, and uppādanirodhavāra) for process metaphysics and momentariness
- [Gal 2003] Noa Gal, Metaphysics of Experience: From the Buddha's Teaching to the Abhidhamma (2003) — Doctrinal analysis of the Process section and momentariness in the Yamaka
